unverified_summary: Nothing here has been tested inside a live boombox, because a boombox belongs to whichever experience you are standing in and any experience can block audio its owner does not own. Three rows are listed as awaiting editor verification for a harder reason: Roblox still lists them free in the Creator Store, but its delivery endpoint refuses the audio file to a request with no session behind it, so public playback cannot be proved from outside a game. Release dates, chart positions and the identity of cover versions are not recorded here at all, because Roblox does not publish them and no other source can be checked against the asset itself.

disagreements.item: How many published song IDs still resolve
disagreements.source_a: Roblox Den lists 2M+ music codes and says its algorithm hides codes that have been removed or deleted
disagreements.source_b: RobloxSong lists 1M+ codes and describes a database that updates in real time to provide working codes only
disagreements.confirmed: Neither claim survives a test. Of 199 unique IDs pulled from four current published lists, 82 no longer resolve as usable audio, and only 56 could be confirmed as served publicly by Roblox.

disagreements.source_a: Published lists label it Stadium Rave by SpongeBob SquarePants
disagreements.source_b: Roblox records the asset as Stadium Rave (A) by Sonoton Music, from the album Clubmix
disagreements.confirmed: Roblox's own asset record stands. The SpongeBob attribution is not supported by anything on the asset page.

disagreements.source_a: Published lists title it Tokyo Drift, which readers take as the Teriyaki Boyz recording
disagreements.source_b: Roblox records the asset as Tokyo Drift by Fumitake Igarashi, from the album DIGITAL PLAYGROUND
disagreements.confirmed: Roblox's own asset record stands. It is a production library track that shares a title, not the film recording.

disagreements.item: Whether Raining Tacos at 142376088 is publicly playable
disagreements.source_a: Every list sampled presents it as a working code, and it is the single most repeated Roblox music code in circulation
disagreements.source_b: Roblox still lists it free in the Creator Store, but its delivery endpoint answers an unauthenticated request with "Authentication required to access Asset"
disagreements.confirmed: Not resolvable from outside a session, so the row is listed as awaiting editor verification rather than being asserted either way.

fakes.claim: ID 1835383046 is Hurt by Nine Inch Nails
fakes.why_wrong: Roblox records that asset as Franche Info by Stephane Daniel Gerard, a production library track distributed through APM Music.
fakes.origin: A song ID list that pasted a library ID under a famous title to fill a row.

fakes.claim: ID 1845015205 is Sigur 1 by Sigur Ros
fakes.why_wrong: Roblox records that asset as Nations United by Cornelus Joh M Cor Bolten, again an APM Music library track.
fakes.origin: The same family of lists, copied between sites without anyone opening the asset page.

fakes.claim: ID 186616625 is Hey Jude by The Beatles
fakes.why_wrong: The asset is not audio. Roblox returns an image asset named Donation 500, so no boombox can play it at all.
fakes.origin: A list that harvested numbers without checking the asset type behind them.

fakes.claim: ID 521116871 is Say So by Doja Cat
fakes.why_wrong: The asset is a Roblox place, not audio. Roblox returns svkoolzam's Place for that number.
The asset is a Roblox place named Legomasterjs's Place. Pasting it into a boombox does nothing.

fakes.claim: ID 1841636346 is a track called Angel
fakes.why_wrong: Roblox records it as Upon a Star a by Alexander Paul Rudd. The title in circulation belongs to no part of the asset record.
fakes.origin: A bulk list of library IDs given invented titles.

changes.what: Page first published. Every ID tested against Roblox's asset, catalogue and delivery endpoints before listing.
Forty widely republished IDs archived as removed or private after testing, rather than dropped.
Three IDs held at Unverified because Roblox lists them free but will not serve the file without a session.

next_change.pattern: Roblox scrubs infringing uploads in waves rather than on a schedule, so an ID can die between one check and the next. Library and distributor uploads survive; re-uploads of commercial records do not.
